messages:
inc-bot: INCIDENT 2460012345 — SEV2: elevated 5xx & latency for KV-backed endpoints in us-west-2. paging oncall @maya @ops-rotation :rotating_light:
maya: on it. seeing alerts in Datadog: kv_store.page_faults spiking, batch_latency p50->p95 jump. linking playbook: <https://redwood.internal/playbooks/kv-batch-mitigation>
sam: confirmed: continuous-batching token counts multiplied for long seqs, KV prefetch grew ~6x; memory pressure triggered paging on some gpus. stacktrace-ish in logs: `kv_prefetch_worker: fetched_pages=614k, active_kv_size=1.9GB, evictions=0`
dmitri: logs show `batch_window_ms=40` was recently increased in canary to reduce latency; that change appears to increase prefix prefetching. suspect combination of larger windows + continuous batching = amplification.
eli: quick customer impact check — 3 tenants with higher QPS (acme-inc, beta-co, dev-pod) show 10-35% error-rate uptick and timeouts on heavy chat flows. acme-inc payments flow hitting 504s.
maya: immediate mitigation plan: 1) revert canary batch_window to baseline for canary hosts 2) enable per-customer prefetch throttle for top 5 tenants 3) deploy micro-canary with reduced max_batch_size 4) monitor 15m. canary flag names: `batch-window-v2`, `kv-prefetch-throttle`, `max-batch-size`
julie: agree. I'll prepare the rollout commands. prefer per-customer overrides first for least blast radius.
eli: acme-inc FYI: contacting AE/CS to let them know we have mitigation in flight. tagging @sales-sre.
dmitri: command snippets: ```
# set per-customer override
redwood-ctl feature-flag set kv-prefetch-throttle --override acme-inc=0.3,beta-co=0.5,dev-pod=0.3
# revert canary
redwood-ctl feature-flag set batch-window-v2 --scope canary=false
# limiter for runtime
redwood-ctl runtime set max-batch-size --value 8 --scope canary
```
maya: executing per-customer throttle now (will post results).
ops-rotation: thanks — I'm prepping a narrow canary for 2 hosts in us-west-2, 5% traffic. will coordinate with julie for config push.
julie: pushing override now: `kv-prefetch-throttle` overrides applied for acme-inc,beta-co,dev-pod. watch for reduced prefetch metrics.
(small pause)
maya: confirmed: prefetch worker fetch rate dropped ~70% for acme-inc within 60s. queue depth normalized. p95 latency improving on canary hosts. :thumbsup:
sam: rolling revert of `batch-window-v2` on canary hosts now. monitoring telemetry streams.
dmitri: quick postmortem note — we saw an edge-case amplification path: when `batch_window` increased and active seq length distribution skews > 1024 tokens, continuous-batching merged prefixes and triggered aggressive prefetch of KV pages beyond configured limits. need a guard.
eli: customer impact summary (so far) — acme-inc: 12% failed requests during spike, now down to 2% after throttle. beta-co: 5%->1%. dev-pod intermittent timeouts clearing. no data loss, only increased latency/504s.
julie: can we flip a temporary hotfix: globally lower `max_batch_size` to 12 and enable `kv-prefetch-safety` to cap prefetch per-shard? propose staged rollout: canary -> 25% -> 100% over 30m if stable.
maya: +1. start canary now for 10% traffic on affected region.
ops-rotation: canary applied. graphs look stable at 8min. starting 25% expansion in 5m.
sam: note: adding an alert rule to detect `kv_prefetch_growth > 2x` in next 24h to catch recurrence.
dmitri: opened a follow-up ticket for runtime guard: add prefetch budget per-shard and refuse prefetch beyond that; also add continuous-batching safety threshold. ticket: RW-ISSUE-4521.
eli: ops note: CS notified, acme-inc ops lead replied they will hold non-critical jobs for 2h. planned customer update at +1h.
maya: handing off to ops-rotation for monitoring and timeline. I'm going offline in 20m — current status: mitigations applied, p95 latency trending down, no new pager activity.
ops-rotation: taking over. summary for next oncall: mitigations = per-customer prefetch throttle, batch-window revert on canary, lowered max_batch_size, staged global rollout in progress. watchlist: `kv_prefetch_worker.fetch_rate`, `batch_latency.p95`, `gpu_mem_pressure`. escalation: ping maya/dmitri if sustained >5m regression.
inc-bot: incident status updated to MONITORING. runbook link: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-prefetch>
ops-rotation: tagging this thread for post-incident writeup. will capture timeline and root-cause. next update in 30m. :white_check_mark:
